task: Add a read-only referential re-validation instrument to the per-project Experience Layer so it can report the valid-rate and drift-rate of its accumulated finding-signals against the current git HEAD.
outcome:
Running `node bin/lattice.js learning_validate` prints, to the terminal, a referential-validity report the operator can read at a glance, for example:

  Experience Layer — referential validity (HEAD 7a52234)
    signals (total):           48
    anchored (have files):     45
    valid (>=1 anchor live):   41
    stale (all anchors gone):   4
    unanchored (no files):      3
    valid-rate:  0.911
    drift-rate:  0.089
  Stale signals (code anchors gone at HEAD):
    - quality||ts|review   anchors: packages/main/src/core/removed-foo.ts
  (advisory, read-only — no gate touched, nothing written)

Adding `--json` instead prints the same numbers as a machine-readable object {head, total, anchored, valid, stale, unanchored, validRate, driftRate, staleSignals[]}. The operator now has a re-runnable instrument that quantifies how much accumulated experience has gone stale.
facts: Derived FindingSignal today keeps only coarse fileKinds (core/finding-signals.ts), not concrete anchor file paths, so per-signal staleness is currently unobservable.
deriveFindingSignalsFromStore(store, opts) reads findings through the store.readFindings port and only persists when opts.projectRoot is given; omitting projectRoot derives without writing.

core/evidence-freshness.ts currentMaterialHash already lists HEAD files via `git ls-tree -r -z HEAD`; this story uses the same git invocation in its own handler and does NOT modify that gate-critical module.
handlers/recall.ts is the established read-only handler template (store read ports only, renders text, writes nothing); registry.ts wires handlers via registry.registerBatch(createXHandlers(ctx)).
Baseline A measured 0.92 finding-level valid rate (8% drift); the signal-level valid-rate produced here is the per-signal analogue.
constraints: The new core/experience-revalidation.ts leaf must import only ./experience-layer-types.js — no fs, no git, no other core module; fileExists is injected.
The learning_validate handler must file no findings, touch no gate, and write nothing (read-only like recall).
No change to the localSignature aggregation key or the signalScore/support math.
anchorFiles must be bounded (capped like exampleFindingIds) to keep the derived cache from growing unboundedly.
unknowns: valid-rate denominator: whether to divide valid signals by all signals or only by anchored signals — resolved in the decision as anchored-only, reporting unanchored separately so the rate is not diluted by signals that never had a file.

how to treat a signal whose anchorFiles are all gone vs partially gone — resolved as stale only when ALL anchors are gone (>=1 live anchor keeps it valid), matching Baseline A's any-file-present rule.
